summary: Earth Jukebox turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into live music. A playhead sweeps across a frame while the app reads the pixels under it: height becomes pitch, color becomes key and tone, edges become rhythm, and the share of intense red becomes musical tension. It lets blind and low vision users, and anyone else, hear sea surface temperature, sea ice, vegetation, fires and air pollution instead of only seeing them. An Explore mode lets users hover, touch or use arrow keys to hear any spot, with spoken style text descriptions. It runs in a browser from a single page with no install.
details:
What it does: pairs each EIC frame with a soundscape generated in real time from that frame's pixels. Users pick a frame (a jukebox track), press play, and either hear a west-to-east sweep or explore single spots.

How it works: the page shrinks the frame to a 96 by 48 grid and measures lightness, warmth, saturation, hue, edge density and the share of strong red. Hue picks the key. Warmth picks the scale (Lydian to minor pentatonic) and timbre. Each grid column becomes one musical step: the most standout pixels become notes whose pitch follows height, loudness follows how much they stand out, and stereo position follows left to right. Edge energy adds shaker ticks. A drone follows brightness. More intense red raises tempo, adds tremolo and a dissonant tone, so warming and fire frames sound tense. Pitch is snapped to a scale so the result stays musical instead of noisy. All audio is synthesized live with the Web Audio API.

Benefits: makes complex Earth science accessible to blind and low-vision users, adds a multi-sensory way for everyone to notice patterns, and works with any image, so new EIC frames need no code changes.

Accessibility: full keyboard control, live text descriptions of each sweep and each explored spot, haptic buzz where supported, reduced-motion support.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas, Web Audio API. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque and IBM Plex Sans/Mono (Google Fonts, SIL OFL).
